_meta.contentStatus: Curated deep-vocabulary collection: precise English words and adopted foreign words, each anchored to its nearest wheel word.

note: The wheel's 63 words are a floor, not a ceiling. Psychologists call the skill of telling similar feelings apart emotional granularity, and research links a finer-grained emotion vocabulary with steadier regulation: each word you know is another shade you can feel in. These words go deeper than the wheel — adopt one and it joins your lexicon.

words.definition: Astonished past speech; the reply you were forming is simply gone.
Confused to a standstill; the problem refuses to take a shape you can start on.
Curiosity leaning forward on its toes, wide open for whatever comes next.
Stopped by beauty or scale; the mind goes quiet instead of racing.
A quiet awareness of depths only suggested, never shown; awe with the mystery left in.
Small, warm, shared comfort — lamplight, company, and nowhere else you need to be.
Glowing pride in the achievement of someone you raised, taught, or love.
Wholehearted delight in someone else's good fortune, with no envy pulling at its edge.
Affection so intense the body clenches; the urge to squeeze what is unbearably dear.
Hope felt as lightness in the chest; it keeps rising without being argued into it.
Longing for a home you cannot return to, or one that never quite existed.
A dull ache of the soul that longs without an object; sorrow with no address.
A soft sorrow at impermanence; things move you more because they are passing.
Weariness at the gap between the world as it is and as it ought to be.
Disappointment you can see in the posture; the visible sag when an outcome lands short.
Lonely with the added sense of being left behind, and that no one is coming.
Disgust arriving as mild nausea; the stomach objects before the mind has its reasons.
Appalled with the breath caught; horrified disbelief that someone actually did it.
Worn numb by too much of what once delighted; the flavor is gone and a faint distaste remains.
Disgust that has settled into hatred; not just recoiling, but wanting it gone.
Resentment gone chronic; it stops seeking repair and rebuilds the world around the grudge.
The sudden torment of seeing your own misery clearly; grief and anger fused, looking for someone to blame.
Wronged and carrying the case for it; anger with a grievance it can cite.
A small, sharp irritation at a slight to your pride; minor, but it lands on the self.
Full anger held under a closed lid — hot, pressurized, and not yet shown.
Fear that walks toward the thing anyway; dread with a date on the calendar.
The gate-closing panic that time is running out on the life you meant to live.
Chased by demands from every side; too hunted to think and too busy to stop.
The restlessness of waiting for someone — checking the window, the door, the road, again.
Distrust learned from experience; you stay pleasant and keep your distance.
